result.title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study
result.summary: Agent skills are documents in which experts write down procedural knowledge, and models increasingly maintain them by rewriting them without feedback. Such rewriting could adapt a skill to the model that uses it or erode the expert knowledge that makes it useful, yet how skills evolve under this feedback-free self-evolution has not been studied. We let models rewrite expert skills round after round without any task, run or judgment and run agents built on the same models with the rewritten skills. Our experiments show that the skills lose value rather than improve, as every model we test performs worse with them on every benchmark, by 15 points on average on SkillsBench after thirty rounds. Sampling each model's prior with skills it writes from the topic alone, we find that rewriting pulls skills toward this prior and gives up first the knowledge outside it. Putting this knowledge back recovers much of the lost pass rate, so an expert's skill is valuable largely for what the model does not write on its own. Building on this insight, SkillDiff marks this knowledge in place and raises the pass rate on SkillsBench by 4.8 points on average without feedback or any change to the skill's text. Project repository: https://github.com/LitaoGuo/How-Self-Evolution-Reshapes-Skills.

AI.brief_summary: 论文系统研究无反馈自我进化如何改变 agent 技能文档：模型在没有任何任务、运行或评判的情况下逐轮重写专家技能，结果各基准性能均下降（SkillsBench 三十轮后平均低 15 分）；分析显示重写把技能拉向模型自身先验并最先丢弃先验之外的知识，据此提出的 SkillDiff 原位标记这部分知识，不改文本、不用反馈即平均提升 4.8 分。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但「无反馈重写使外部知识向模型先验坍缩、先失去先验外信息」的观察，可能可供核查 latent 状态中视觉细节被语言先验吞没的同类失效，以及保留证据类信息的标记式做法。
